what: The brief's headline case — 250 label applications dumped at once — driven through the deployed batch UI on the build that carries the 2026-08-13/14 changes (shared verdict summary, relocated batch decisions, rebuilt bold spot-check crop, bottler lead-in fix, empty-fields guard fix). Re-run because the standing batch-ui-250.json evidence predates all of them.
how: 250 rows assembled in the browser from the twelve bundled sample applications (each row under its own filename) and dropped on the batch dropzone as a CSV plus 250 image files. Same client path as a real drop: per-image deskew, 250 object URLs, filename pairing, streaming table. Counts below are read from the exported report, not from the table, so they are exact rather than eyeballed.

timing_caveat.issue: The browser pane was not displayed for this run (document.hidden === true), which suspends the renderer between interactions. Real elapsed time was therefore much longer than the figure above, and the app's own clock advanced only while the tab was awake.
timing_caveat.what_the_number_is: 139.1s is ACTIVE processing time as measured by the page, not wall time on a foregrounded tab.
timing_caveat.why_it_is_still_worth_recording: It agrees closely with the 146.5s recorded by the earlier, independent 250-row run in batch-ui-250.json under the same constraint — two runs, two builds, ~5% apart.
timing_caveat.what_would_settle_it: One run with the browser pane displayed. Not done here; the number is reported as approximate rather than dressed up.

note_on_the_review_everything_start: All 250 rows land in Needs review before the bold pass runs, because past 60 rows that pass is opt-in and a row whose bold was never examined must not show a green tick. That is deliberate. See batch-72-optin.json for the measured effect of clicking Check bold type at 72 rows: 39 of 56 eligible rows resolved by measurement, 17 left for a human glance.
